notes: AUDITABLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for every exchange session this platform generates. Downstream code
(coverage denominators, gap detection, and the Phase 4 leakage firewall's feature cutoffs) is
validated AGAINST the sessions produced from this file, so a wrong entry here is invisible by
construction. Read it as data, not as an implementation detail: every field is meant to be
checkable against a published exchange calendar by a human, without reading any C#.
WHAT IS A RULE AND WHAT IS DATA. Only the statutory, mechanically-defined holidays are rules
(nth-weekday, fixed-date-with-weekend-observance, Good Friday from the Gregorian Easter
computation). EVERYTHING an exchange decided rather than derived is data: unscheduled closures
(9/11, Hurricane Sandy, national days of mourning), unscheduled early closes, the year a holiday
entered the calendar (MLK 1998, Juneteenth 2022), every early-close wall-clock time, and — added
2026-08-01 — every date a venue trades a SHORTENED session on a day the holiday rules say it is
shut (`partialSessionSets`). A purely rule-based generator invents sessions on days the market
was shut AND deletes sessions on days it was open; this split exists to prevent both.
CONFIDENCE. Every unscheduled entry carries a `confidence`. 'high' = widely documented and
cross-checkable, or measured directly off the wire; 'medium' = documented but the venue-by-venue
detail is inferred; 'unverified' = believed correct but NOT confirmed against a published exchange
calendar — grep for it and check it before trusting any study whose window includes that date.
PARTIAL SESSIONS. A `partialSessionSets` entry names a date the venue's holiday rules (or its
closure set) say it is SHUT, but on which it in fact traded a shortened session ending at `close`.
Only the session labels in `sessions` are generated for that date; every other session template on
the calendar is suppressed. This is the only mechanism that can turn a rule-derived holiday back
into a trading date, and it is per-date DATA on purpose: CME equity index trades a shortened
session on most US holidays, is fully shut on Christmas and New Year, and on Good Friday does one
or the other depending on whether the monthly employment report falls that day — no rule expresses
that. A partial-session entry on a date that is NOT otherwise closed is rejected at load time, so a
mis-projected future holiday date fails loudly instead of inventing a session.
TRADING-DATE ATTRIBUTION for a partial session: it belongs to the trading date it ENDS on, i.e.
the holiday itself. IBKR's own schedule feed rolls these fragments forward onto the NEXT trading
date's refDate (it did so for 2026-07-03 and did not for 2025-01-20 — its convention changed
during 2025). This platform cannot follow that: two sessions would then share one (calendar,
trading date, label), which research.sessions forbids, and an ES bar at 09:00 CT on Thanksgiving
would be attributed to the Friday. The date a session ends on is the date it belongs to.
AN UNSCHEDULED EARLY CLOSE IS PER VENUE, AND ITS TIME IS APPLIED TO EVERY SESSION TEMPLATE ON THAT
venue that takes early closes. That is why NYSE_EXTENDED is its own venue rather than a second
calendar on the NYSE one: the 2015 leap-second close at 19:30 ET shortened the extended session and
left the regular session entirely alone, and an entry for it in the set NYSE RTH reads would not
shorten RTH — it would LENGTHEN it from 16:00 to 19:30. Two venues that share every rule set and
differ only in their unscheduled data are cheap; a shared set that silently re-times the wrong
session is not.
SESSION TEMPLATES MAY BE DATED. A session row can carry `effectiveFrom`/`effectiveTo` when a venue
genuinely changed a session's hours (the VIX index day leg has done so three times). Rows sharing
a label must tile the calendar's whole lifetime with no gap and no overlap — enforced at load time
— so exactly one row applies to every trading date and the (calendar, trading date, label) key
stays unique.
HOW THE 2026-08-01 ENTRIES WERE ESTABLISHED. Everything marked 'high' below with a
`source: tws-schedule` note came from IBKR's own published trading schedule, read off a live
paper TWS socket (server version 223) with `reqHistoricalData(whatToShow="SCHEDULE")`, which
returns one (start, end, refDate) triple per session in the contract's own time zone. That is the
venue schedule as the data provider distributes it, not an inference from where bars happen to
stop; where a claim could be cross-checked against actual 1-minute bar spans it was, and the two
agreed. Requests were read-only.
BUMP generatorVersion ON ANY CHANGE to this file. SessionGenerator.GeneratorVersion must match it
(a unit test enforces this), and research.sessions.generator_version records it per row, so a
regenerated calendar is distinguishable from a stale one.
TIMES ARE EXCHANGE-LOCAL WALL CLOCK in the calendar's IANA time zone. They are never offsets.
SessionClock converts; nothing else in the platform is permitted to.

US_MARKET.name: New Year's Day
US_MARKET.note: Deliberately NOT saturdayToFriday. NYSE Rule 7.2 excepts New Year's Day from the Saturday rule: Jan 1 2005, Jan 1 2011 and Jan 1 2022 all fell on a Saturday and the preceding Fridays (Dec 31) were full trading days.

US_MARKET.note: Two days before Gregorian Easter Sunday (Meeus/Butcher). Verified against 2001-04-13, 2012-04-06, 2024-03-29, 2025-04-18, 2026-04-03.

US_MARKET.note: Dec 24, only when Dec 25 falls Mon-Fri. Matches the 2012-2015, 2018-2020, 2024, 2025 early closes and the absence of one in 2016, 2017, 2021-2023.

CME_UNSCHEDULED.note: OVERRIDDEN by partialSessionSets.CME_EQUITY_INDEX, which records that Globex equity index traded 17:00 CT the prior evening to 08:30 CT rather than closing. The two coexist the same way a holiday rule coexists with a partial session: the closure records that the day was a market-wide closure for this venue, the partial entry records the shortened session it traded anyway. Removing this row instead would defeat the load-time guard that refuses a partial session on a day the venue was otherwise open — the guard that makes the hand-projected 2027 holiday dates safe to ship.

So this 2018 entry is more likely a shortened session too. Nothing was observed for 2018 (IBKR's published schedule for ES only reaches 2021, and only distinguishes shortened sessions from 2022-11-24 — see the CME_EQUITY_INDEX notes), and an omitted session under-states a denominator rather than manufacturing one, so it stays a closure until somebody can measure it.

NYSE_EXTENDED.note: Every RULE is shared with NYSE, and that is measured rather than assumed: IBKR's published SPY schedule returns 4,166 sessions over 2010-01-04..2026-07-31 and every one of their dates is a date the NYSE calendar already generates — no session on a holiday, none on Hurricane Sandy (2012-10-29/30) or either day of mourning (2018-12-05, 2025-01-09), and the 34 dates it reports at 17:00 are exactly the 34 the US_MARKET early-close rules produce, with no extra and none missing. Hence no partialSessionSet: unlike CME equity index, this venue never trades a shortened session on a day its own rules call it shut. Only the UNSCHEDULED early-close set differs, because only that set carries an explicit wall-clock time — see the note block above.

CBOE.note: Cboe follows the NYSE holiday and unscheduled-closure schedule, including both Hurricane Sandy days. The 1997-10-27 circuit-breaker close applied to Cboe too, but the exact Cboe index-option halt time is not recorded here, so no unscheduled early close is asserted — an unasserted early close leaves a normal-length session, which shows up as a visible low-coverage afternoon rather than as silently discarded data. No partialSessionSet: Cboe is genuinely shut on the US holidays CME trades short. Measured 2026-08-01 — the SPX and VIX index schedules carry exactly 752 sessions over 2023-08-02..2026-07-31, the same count as NYSE trading days, with no holiday session among them.

CME.note: Differs from NYSE/Cboe on Hurricane Sandy: CME's electronic markets stayed open on 2012-10-29 and 2012-10-30 while the NYSE and Cboe were shut, so those dates are absent from CME_UNSCHEDULED. The 1996 blizzard entry is likewise absent (a New York weather closure). It also differs on nearly every US holiday: Globex equity index trades a SHORTENED session rather than closing, which partialSessionSet now carries. Only Christmas Day and New Year's Day are consistently full closures (measured: Dec 24 2024/2025 close 12:15 CT with no evening reopen, and the next session starts 17:00 CT on Christmas Day itself; Dec 31 is a full 16:00 CT session with no evening reopen, and the next starts 17:00 CT on Jan 1).

calendars.description: NYSE/ARCA cash equities regular session. SPY's calendar.

The full NYSE/ARCA cash-equity trading day — 04:00-20:00 ET — which NESTS the 09:30-16:00 regular session on the NYSE calendar. SPY's second calendar, and the fix for 570 minutes a day of real data that no session described. Measured 2026-08-01 off live TWS: SPY (conId 756733, US/Eastern) reports tradingHours 0400-2000 against liquidHours 0930-1600; IBKR's published schedule returns 4,166 sessions over 2010-01-04..2026-07-31, of which 4,131 are 04:00-20:00, 34 are 04:00-17:00 and one is 04:00-19:30; and a useRth=false 1-minute TRADES request returns exactly 960 bars a day running 04:00..19:59 ET with no minute missing. Latent before this entry only because both shipped SPY jobs are useRth=true — the moment one is not, every extended session reported as an audit hole.

sessions.label: GTH
sessions.note: ONE session spanning the regular one, not a pre-market row plus a post-market row. That is forced, not preferred: research.sessions permits only the labels RTH and GTH and keys them UNIQUE (calendar, trading_date, label), so two GTH rows on one calendar and trading date cannot be stored, and the load-time tiling check rejects two undated rows sharing a label before it ever gets that far. CME_ES is the precedent and SessionMinutes.DistinctMinutes unions rather than sums so the nesting cannot double-count; here the nesting is across two calendar KEYS (NYSE + NYSE_EXTENDED) rather than within one, and the union sweep is calendar-blind, so a full SPY day is 960 expected minutes and not 960 + 390. openDayOffset is 0: unlike Cboe's option GTH and the Globex day, this session opens after midnight on its own trading date. The 17:00 early close is MEASURED, not the 20:00 close minus the 3 hours the regular session loses — the VIX day leg is a live counter-example where the early close did not move with the regular one. 780 bars running 04:00..16:59 ET on 2025-07-03, 2025-11-28 and 2025-12-24, and 04:48..16:59 on 2009-12-24.

calendars.note: effectiveFrom is 2010-01-04 — the first trading date of the first calendar year in which every row IBKR publishes for SPY is a real schedule — and NOTHING is asserted before it, deliberately. The feed reaches 1998 and claims 04:00-20:00 throughout, but that stretch is a weekday FILL: it returns sessions on Christmas Day 1998, on July 4 2000-2006 and on New Year's Day 1999-2004, reports every half day from 1999 to 2005 as a full 20:00 close, emits 09:30-16:00 regular-session rows on actual 2006/2007 holidays, and emits zero-length 16:00-16:00 rows on 2007-11-23, 2007-12-24 and 2009-11-27. The bars say the same thing POSITIVELY rather than by absence — the extended session's first traded minute walks earlier over the years: exactly 08:00 ET with exactly 720 bars on 2005-01-04, 2005-02-02 and 2005-03-01 (that is an open, not three coincidences), ~07:25 later in 2005, ~06:25 in 2007, 04:15 by 2008-03-05, 04:00 exactly by 2011-03-16. So the window genuinely moved, and dated rows were considered and rejected: modelling 04:00 back through 2005 would over-expect by up to 240 minutes a day, which is the direction that MANUFACTURES gaps, and the earlier shapes cannot be pinned because a trade-driven first bar is only an upper bound on the open. The 20:00 close IS measured back to 2005-06-01 (last bar 19:59 on every sampled date), but a close without an established open is not a session. KNOWN RESIDUAL: a useRth=false SPY job reaching before 2010 is audited against the 390-minute regular session alone, which under-states rather than manufacturing, and is the same direction as CME_ES having no partial entries before 2022-11-24.

calendars.description: Cboe index OPTION regular session (SPX, SPXW). Closes 15:15 CT = 16:15 ET — fifteen minutes after the cash equity close, on full and half days alike. This is the option session and nothing else: the SPX and VIX INDEX levels are computed on different schedules and have their own calendars (CBOE_SPX_RTH, CBOE_VIX_RTH). Using this key for an index level is the defect that made 100% of SPX index sessions report succeeded_but_absent.

Cboe Global Trading Hours for SPX/SPXW index OPTIONS: 19:15 CT the PRIOR calendar day through 08:25 CT on the trading date (20:15-09:25 ET). effectiveFrom is the near-24x5 GTH expansion; before it no overnight index-option session existed, and generating one would manufacture sessions that never happened. The 19:15 CT open is runtime-verified — docs/research/ibkr-data-capability-matrix.md records useRTH=0 SPX bars starting 19:15 US/Central on the prior calendar day, and the 20:15-09:15 ET session in the pacing/limits section.

sessions.label: GTH
sessions.note: The close was 08:15 until 2026-08-01 and that was wrong by ten minutes, so 13:15Z-13:25Z on every trading date carried real SPX option quotes belonging to no session. Measured two independent ways against live TWS: contractDetails for SPXW 260807C06400000 (conId 889088590) reports tradingHours '20260802:1915-20260803:0825', and a 1-minute BID_ASK useRTH=0 request for the same contract has its last overnight bar stamped 08:24 CT on both 2026-07-30 and 2026-07-31 (a 1-minute bar stamped 08:24 covers 08:24-08:25), followed by a six-minute break to the 08:30 CT regular open. appliesEarlyClose is false because a GTH session ENDS in the morning, before any afternoon early close could shorten it. An early close on trading date D truncates D's RTH, not D's GTH. Whether Cboe suppresses the overnight session on a holiday EVENING (which would remove the GTH session belonging to the next trading date) is not asserted here — see eveningSessionClosedOn.

calendars.description: The SPX INDEX LEVEL dissemination window — the session SPX index bars actually land in, which is the US cash equity session and NOT the 15:15 CT option close. Measured 2026-08-01 off live TWS: contractDetails for SPX IND (conId 416904) reports tradingHours and liquidHours '0830-1500' US/Central, IBKR's published schedule returns 752 sessions of 08:30-15:00 CT over 2023-08-02..2026-07-31 with 08:30-12:00 CT on half days, and five consecutive useRTH=1 1-minute TRADES sessions returned exactly 390 bars each running 08:30..14:59 CT. There is NO overnight leg: a useRTH=0 '2 D' request returned 780 bars = 2 x 390, all inside the day window.

sessions.label: RTH
sessions.note: IBKR's published schedule reports the SPX index close as 15:15 CT from at least 2001-08-07 to 2013-03-08, then 15:00 CT from 2013-03-11 (the boundary falls on a weekend, so these two rows tile the calendar exactly). One exception inside this window is knowingly NOT modelled: 2011-03-28 alone is reported at 15:00 CT, with 15:15 either side of it. A single-day row for one date fifteen years ago is not worth the entry; the cost is a 15-minute over-expectation on that one date, which is the direction that can manufacture a gap, so it is named here rather than left to be discovered. This row is also what the platform assumed for ALL of history before 2026-08-01, so nothing regresses for dates before 2013. Half-day closes before 2011 are reported by IBKR as full sessions, which is a fill rather than a fact; 12:15 is carried over from CBOE_INDEX_RTH for that stretch.

sessions.label: RTH
sessions.note: 08:30-15:00 CT = 09:30-16:00 ET, i.e. exactly the NYSE cash session, and 12:00 CT = 13:00 ET on a half day, exactly the NYSE half day. Half-day closes measured at 12:00 CT on 2023-11-24, 2024-07-03, 2024-11-29, 2024-12-24, 2025-07-03, 2025-11-28 and 2025-12-24.

calendars.description: The VIX INDEX LEVEL day session. Measured 2026-08-01 off live TWS: contractDetails for VIX IND (conId 13455763) reports tradingHours and liquidHours '0830-1600' US/Central for the day leg, and IBKR's published schedule gives the three historical shapes below. Cross-checked against real bars rather than trusted: a 1-minute TRADES useRTH=0 request returned 765 bars on 2022-04-21 and 2022-04-22 with the last at 15:14 CT, and 810 bars on 2022-04-25 and 2022-04-26 with the last at 15:59 CT — the schedule's 15:15 -> 16:00 change on exactly that weekend, seen independently in the data.

sessions.label: RTH
sessions.note: IBKR reports 08:30-15:15 CT continuously from at least 2001-08-07 to 2011-03-25. Identical to CBOE_INDEX_RTH, which is what VIX was measured against before 2026-08-01, so this row is exactly the previous behaviour.

sessions.label: RTH
sessions.note: A real 171-session interval in IBKR's published schedule, not a data artefact: the one half day inside it (2011-11-25) is reported at 12:00 CT, consistent with the 15:00 CT regular close, and the shape reverts on 2011-11-30. Modelled rather than skipped because skipping it would over-expect by 15 minutes on 171 sessions, which is the direction that manufactures gaps.

sessions.label: RTH
sessions.note: Half days measured at 12:15 CT throughout this window, from 2012-07-03 to 2021-11-26.

sessions.label: RTH
sessions.note: The current shape, and the one that matters: 08:30-16:00 CT = 09:30-17:00 ET, 450 minutes, 45 minutes past the Cboe option close. Measured on the wire (810 bars/day = 360 overnight + 450 day; last day bar 15:59 CT). Half days STAY at 12:15 CT — measured on 2022-11-25, 2023-07-03, 2023-11-24, 2024-07-03, 2024-11-29, 2024-12-24, 2025-07-03, 2025-11-28 and 2025-12-24 — so the early close is NOT the regular close minus a fixed offset.

calendars.description: The VIX INDEX LEVEL overnight session — 02:15 CT to 08:15 CT on the trading date's OWN calendar date, which is a completely different window from the 19:15-08:25 CT index-OPTION session in CBOE_INDEX_GTH. Expecting the option window over VIX index bars is the original cry-wolf defect InstrumentCalendars was created to fix; leaving it unmodelled instead left the VIX series permanently unreconciled, which is the same failure in the other direction. Measured 2026-08-01: contractDetails for VIX IND reports tradingHours and liquidHours '0215-0815' US/Central as a separate leg from '0830-1600', IBKR's published schedule returns one such leg on every one of the 752 trading dates over 2023-08-02..2026-07-31 (half days included, unshortened), and a useRTH=0 1-minute TRADES request returns 360 overnight bars running 02:15..08:14 CT. effectiveFrom is the first date IBKR's schedule reports the leg at all; nothing is asserted before it.

sessions.label: GTH
sessions.note: The leg opened at 02:00 CT from 2016-04-15 to 2019-04-29 and at 02:15 CT from 2019-04-30. Both are IBKR's published schedule; the change is on consecutive trading days.

sessions.label: GTH
sessions.note: openDayOffset is 0, NOT -1: unlike Cboe's option GTH and the Globex day, the VIX overnight leg starts after midnight on its own trading date, so its trading date and its exchange-local calendar date are the same. appliesEarlyClose is false because the leg ends in the morning — and it is measured to run unshortened on half days, not merely assumed to.

calendars.description: CME Globex E-mini S&P 500. The Globex day for trading date D runs 17:00 CT on D-1 through 16:00 CT on D (recorded as the GTH row); RTH is the 08:30-15:15 CT equity-index regular session nested inside it. effectiveFrom is the ES contract launch.

sessions.label: GTH
sessions.note: Globex reopens at 17:00 CT on holiday evenings (e.g. the Christmas Day evening session belonging to Dec 26), so this row is generated whenever its TRADING DATE is a trading day, regardless of what the prior calendar day was. The 16:00-17:00 CT daily maintenance halt is the gap between one day's close and the next day's open, so it needs no separate representation.

sessions.label: RTH
sessions.note: IBKR reports ES liquidHours as 0830-1600 CT, 45 minutes longer than this row. Left at 15:15 CT — the published CME equity-index regular session — because it is deliberately under-stated rather than over-stated, and because ES's instrument mapping claims the GTH row too, which nests this one, so the union of expected minutes is identical either way. partialSessionSets never lists RTH: on a shortened holiday session there is no regular session, only the Globex fragment, and IBKR emits no daily bar for those dates either.
